title: The fibres of a base change are the base changes of the fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:S'\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $X'=X\times_SS'$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$, let $s'\in S'$ and $s=g(s')$, and let $r:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s')$ be the map induced by $g$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $X'_{s'}=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$ be the fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre] of $f$ at $s$ and of $f'$ at $s'$, with projections $\iota:X_s\to X$, $\pi:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, $\iota':X'_{s'}\to X'$, $\pi':X'_{s'}\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$. Then there is a unique morphism $h:X'_{s'}\to X_s$ with $\iota\circ h=g'\circ\iota'$ and $\pi\circ h=\operatorname{Spec}(r)\circ\pi'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and the square formed by $h$, $\pi'$, $\pi$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(r):\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is cartesian: $(X'_{s'},h,\pi')$ is a fibre product $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s')$.
